source: TASKS.md 'In progress' on ccr-6a61f25c-wn80ii (da2878ec) and each lane's branch head. The DRI edits this file; run tutorial/tools/build.py to re-embed it. Each lane's 'group' sets its heading in section 14 (groups appear in first-seen order).

T10.title: Minimal pair: H = 16 at T = 4 versus T = 5
T10.what: The smallest place where the deterministic calculation starts losing ground to sampling. Which error patches appear at T = 5?
T10.latest: PASS of its pre-registered test at H = 16, T = 5 (squared error at most .23 of sampling's on every seed), independently confirmed on fresh models by T379 (ledger H-E16, scoped). Deterministic quadrature over fixed Sobol lines, exact along each line; ARC acceptance unknown. Finding: the new T = 5 mistakes sit mainly where all inputs are negative, and the gain falls like 1 / error rate (Figure 5).

T379.title: Independent fresh-model check of T10
T379.what: Re-test T10's T = 5 pass on fresh models, because its sign groupings were chosen on the test seeds.
T379.latest: Passed: T10's frozen estimator beats sampling on 5 fresh H = 16, T = 5 retrains (squared error at most .14 of sampling's; 320 of 320 runs with alternative rules below 1). Now ledger row H-E16, confirmed and scoped: deterministic fixed-line quadrature (ARC acceptance unknown), clean models, compute counted in network-run equivalents; 10-35x slower than sampling in wall-clock time.

T11.title: The same frozen recipe at T = 6
T11.what: Climb the ladder: apply T10's frozen quadrature recipe one step further, at T = 6.
T11.latest: Narrow FAIL: 9 of 10 checks pass. The pre-registered gain law (1 / error rate) predicted all 10 cells. Next lever: a lower-variance integrand (T380).

T380.title: A lower-variance integrand for T = 6
T380.what: Reduce how much the per-face contributions vary, the lever the 1 / error-rate law points to.
T380.latest: FAIL, as predicted, for a control-variate integrand. The frozen T10 quadrature roughly matches sampling at T = 10 on DEV3 (squared-error ratio .97 at 64k runs, 1.15 at 16k) but does not beat it. Next: T389, a weight-derived error predictor.

T389.title: A weight-derived error predictor for T = 10
T389.what: Next lever after T380: predict from the weights where the errors are, to cut the quadrature's variance.
T389.latest: Stopped by its pre-set 64k line (DEV3 1.215); .738 at 16k. Superseded: the budget study T429 and the sealed HP5 run T431 showed that the T10 recipe passes the strict bar from about 1e6 runs per model (H-E17).

T391.title: One global importance-weighted rule at T = 10
T391.what: Follow-up to T389: a single weight-derived allocation rule for the fixed lines at T = 10. A sealed HP5 run follows only if it passes.
T391.latest: Stopped by its pre-set line: DEV3 .859 [.659, 1.078] at 16k and .880 [.620, 1.165] at 64k, intervals crossing 1; HP5 left untouched for T431.

T46.title: Exact ladder at H = 16: T = 5 and 6, then a hybrid
T46.what: Resumed by the owner: exact rows at T = 5/6, then a hybrid exact/estimated method. Correction to the earlier record: on 10-17 only seeds 0-1 were computed exactly at T = 5, not 0-4.
T46.latest: Exact counts done for all leaderboard models at T = 2-4 (and T = 5 on seeds 0-3). The hybrid of exact regions and tracing FAILED, as pre-registered and predicted: no admissible split at T = 5, 6 or 10 within budget.

T86+T111.title: Training the missing ladder sizes
T86+T111.what: Resumed by the owner: train ladder sizes AlgZoo lacks and a better-trained H = 4, T = 4 network.
T86+T111.latest: New ladder sizes trained and matching AlgZoo (e.g. 7 neurons, 3 numbers). Better training of the 4-neuron, 4-step rung FAILED every attempt (best ~.60); whether T or undertraining is the cause is inconclusive.

T393.title: Compiled walk: real wall-clock cost
T393.what: Measure the walk methods' actual run time, not only arithmetic counts (they were 10-35x slower than sampling in wall-clock time).
T393.latest: At H = 16, T = 5 the compiled walk also wins on real wall-clock time (time ratio .09-.30 against an equally compiled sampler at equal error). At T = 10 it loses at 16k runs and is inconclusive at 64k.

T429.title: Does the walk quadrature improve with budget at T = 10?
T429.latest: Yes, against the pre-registered 'flat' prediction: on DEV3 F falls about x.75 per 4x budget; the strict bar holds (interval below 1) from 1e6 runs per model for both recipes. deterministic, ARC acceptance unknown.

T431.title: Sealed HP5 run of the walk quadrature at T = 10
T431.latest: Strict pass on a sealed, never-used panel of 100 retrains, scored once by the independent scorer: F .540 [.343, .762] at 4e6 runs per model (plain-sampling control 1.015).

T449.title: A weight-derived bound on the line-averaging error?
T449.latest: No: every bound family tried is infinite or hundreds of times looser than the actual error, because a line's answer has creases and jumps where it grazes region boundaries. Closing it would need cells at the scale of the exact regions.

T423.title: Walk quadrature on wider networks
T423.latest: Interim: at 24 and 32 neurons (T = 10) the strict bar holds at 4k, 16k and 64k runs (F .17-.49); the prediction that wider is harder is refuted at 16-32 neurons.

T434.title: Walk quadrature on noisy copies and on the target itself
T434.latest: H-E17's open scope: weight-noised copies and the target model M_16,10.

T442.title: Other fixed line sets
T442.latest: Does H-E17 depend on the particular fixed line set?

T370.title: Rare events: fix the simplified treatment of the smaller inputs
T370.what: Replace the closure that pins the 7 smaller inputs at one value with a real integral over their exact law, the cause T363 and T369 point to for the remaining rare-event failures.
T370.latest: Stage 1 PASSED with a deterministic cubature closure (Q16): the worst network fixed (.79 / .70), controls 12 of 12 within 2x, the both-gaps-large event 25 of 29 within 2x; cost 2.8-4.6e7 runs per model. A sealed stage 2 on 8 untouched pairs is running.

T371.title: Rare events on weight-noised copies
T371.what: Does the confirmed far-gap estimator (H-R1) stay within 2x when noise is added to the weights, as in ARC's noisy copies?
T371.latest: Passed: the rare-event estimator holds on weight-noised copies (128 of 144 within 2x). Every point where three-way near-ties carry less than half the event is within 2x (110 of 110); whether near-ties dominate depends on the model and the threshold. Follow-up T388 is running.

T388.title: Rare events where three-way near-ties dominate
T388.what: Follow-up to T371: the remaining misses on noisy copies sit where three-way near-ties carry most of the event.
T388.latest: The graded rule fixes all 16 former misses on noisy copies (143 of 144 within 2x overall), breaking 1 former hit.

T372.title: Which weights cause a rare mistake?
T372.what: An exact derivative of a rare-error probability with respect to all 432 weights, read off the gate crossings along the exact walks. Plain sampling of a 0/1 event has no unbiased finite-variance derivative.
T372.latest: The deterministic gradient failed (2 of 12 directions). A sampling-class gradient along the exact lines works and points to the n6/n7 comparator balance; independently confirmed by T385.

T385.title: Independent check of the rare-event gradient
T385.what: Re-check T372's sampling-class gradient and its n6/n7 mechanism with independent code.
T385.latest: Independent check with its own line family: all 3 pre-set lines pass (sampling-class gradient). It supports T372's sampling-class result.

T373.title: Certified rare-event probability inside the event's own cone
T373.what: Count the linear regions inside the region of input space where a far-gap mistake can happen. The idea is only viable if that count stays small (at most 2e8 projected at 10 steps); the first run decides.
T373.latest: Stopped: counting regions inside the event's cone is out of reach at 10 steps. The certified-bound work continued with tighter bounds and neuron splitting (T398, T400, T416).

T390.title: Event-guided branch and bound
T390.what: Kill test: follow only the few prefixes where the rare event is still possible (T373).
T390.latest: Stopped: event-guided branch and bound projects about 2.1e8 nodes, above its 1e7 line.

T386.title: De-aliased deterministic rare-event gradient
T386.what: Fix the fixed-line aliasing that sank T372's deterministic gradient.
T386.latest: A de-aliased deterministic gradient still fails its gate (6 of 12 directions, against 80% needed).

T436.title: Dominating-point importance sampling (sampling-class)
T436.latest: Applying Bai, Huang, Lam and Zhao (2020): estimates the target's far-gap mistake at 1.45e-10 (7.9% relative error) with about 1e5x less compute than plain sampling.

T454.title: Honest intervals for importance sampling
T454.latest: Within 2x on all 15 blind points (T453: 14/15), but the error bars are honest on only 12 of 15 (14 needed). A version scored on fresh points runs (T456).

T401+T407+T427.title: Safe-use rating
T401+T407+T427.latest: 'If the top numbers differ by at least X, the error rate is Y': works on some networks, partly on the target (T401, T407); on a 24-neuron network it works for the rarer conditions instead (T427, interim).

H-R3.title: Locating and repairing a rare mistake
H-R3.latest: A 12-weight edit makes the target's far-gap mistake about 17-19x rarer at about .011 points of accuracy; 0 of 40 random edits of the same size succeed (T402, T410). Removing all such mistakes is not possible: repairs turn rare mistakes into common ones (T411).

T400+T416.title: Certified upper bound on a rare mistake
T400+T416.latest: Sampling: P(far-gap mistake at gap 2.5) = 1.55e-10, at most 4.2e-10 with confidence 1 - 1e-6 (T400). Rigorous: on one section of inputs, triple (1,8,2), at most about 1.36e-11 (T416, provisional until the geometry audit T420). All 17 sampled mistakes sit on triple (9,3,2): about 2 million pieces, about 5 CPU-days to charge (T398, T400).

T418+T455.title: The late-section obstruction
T418+T455.latest: T418: the late sections looked blocked, but the blocker was the splitting rule, not the bounds; a better rule projects about 2e6-2e7 pieces per section. A rigorous version runs (T455), so a guarantee over all inputs may be feasible.

T345.title: Feed-forward version of the task
T345.what: Find the simplest plain ReLU network that sees all 10 numbers at once and reaches M_16,10's accuracy (>= .95), fewest layers first; then attempt the challenge on it with exact tools versus sampling at equal compute.
T345.latest: Simplest all-at-once network reaching .95: one hidden layer of 128 (2,560 weights), mostly pairwise comparators; as many pieces as the RNN. Random circle walks are sampling-class; fixed circle sets are deterministic, ARC acceptance unknown. No deductive method was found (T408).

T387.title: Fixed (deterministic) circle sets on the feed-forward network
T387.what: Replace T345's random great circles by fixed point sets.
T387.latest: Fixed Halton circle sets give F mean .15, all below 1 (deterministic, ARC acceptance unknown); fixed symmetric and lattice sets fail. Re-checked independently by T394.

T352.title: Quantised activations (binary, int4, int8) and discrete inputs
T352.what: Retrain M_16,10 with quantisation-aware training so each neuron takes only a few values. The network then becomes a finite-state machine, and an exact dynamic programme over reachable states may beat sampling.
T352.latest: Negative, scoped to the tested networks: int4 reaches .95 only at 64 neurons, and its hidden states are almost unique per input, so the exact state-by-state calculation is infeasible; binary networks stay at .43-.52 even at 64 neurons.

T392.title: Chunked-input RNN
T392.what: An RNN that reads k numbers per step (k = 1, 2, 5, 10), between the 10-step RNN and the all-at-once network.
T392.latest: The challenge gets easier as the network reads more numbers per step, but almost all the gain is between 5 and 10 numbers per step, and it comes from cheaper propagation, not from fewer regions.

T394.title: Independent check of the all-at-once results
T394.latest: Independent check of the all-at-once network: all 10 fixed Halton sets beat sampling (F mean .19-.37) on 6 fresh networks; two details of T345/T387 corrected (Halton is not clearly better than random circles; 3 of 6 seeds stayed below .95 at the shorter training).

T419.title: Other tasks on the same network shape
T419.latest: Quick screen: 24 of 29 candidate tasks reach at least .70 and go on to full training.

T421.title: Bigger networks
T421.latest: 16 neurons cannot do 20 numbers (.46); 32 can (.93). From 16 to 24 neurons at T = 10, accuracy jumps from ~.88 to ~.99, so errors are ~10x rarer.

T433+T444.title: A mini language model
T433+T444.latest: Two small languages and 36 baseline models (T433). Attention that keeps our exact methods usable matches standard attention on the bracket language (T444). Estimating, rare-mistake and guarantee streams run (T445-T447).

T395.title: GPU census at 1e10 inputs
T395.what: Repeat the gate-pattern census with 10x more inputs, to sharpen how fast the probability-carrying patterns grow.
T395.latest: With 1e10 inputs, the effective number of error patterns grows about x3.9, x3.2, x2.7 per step at 7-10 steps, still falling: close to the ~3x 'revival' line, far below the 25-44x growth of raw regions.

T443.title: Re-check of the small-rung calculator
T443.latest: A bug re-check of the region calculator used on small rungs changed no verdicts.

T291.title: Strict bar with a different representation
T291.what: Track the hidden state as low-degree polynomials of Gaussian inputs, computed from the weights with explicit error terms: no sampling, no fitted closure. H-S1 says the strict bar needs a new way of representing the state; this is one.
T291.latest: Stopped, scoped to degree <= 5: even the best degree-1..5 polynomial fit of the TRUE output scores picks the right answer only 13-40% of the time, so this representation cannot work at these degrees, whatever the propagation. Follow-up T375 is in progress.

T375.title: Strict bar: a compressed tensor-train representation
T375.what: Follow-up to T291: represent the network's state in a compressed tensor-train class, starting with an oracle gate (can the class even represent the true logits well enough?).
T375.latest: Stopped: the best tensor-train fit of the TRUE output scores picks the right answer only 35-40% of the time, against 87-96% needed. The polynomial-representation line is closed at these budgets.

T3.title: Symbols from the clock neurons' gate switches
T3.what: Describe the network as a symbolic system whose symbols are the rotating neurons' on/off switches; ceiling test on 18 models.
T3.latest: Failed its ceiling test: bias -.61 to +.46 pp, within .08 pp on 7 of 18 models. Two opposite biases cancel, and the clock neurons are no better than random gate sets. Follow-up T376 is in progress.

T376.title: Clock-switch symbols with consistent smaller inputs
T376.what: Follow-up to T3: make the smaller inputs consistent with each symbol, and run a ceiling test with sample-fitted tables.
T376.latest: Failed its ceiling test: bias -.001 to +.958 pp, within .08 pp on 1 of 18 models; setting the smaller inputs to their average given the symbol brings back E27's positive bias. Third failure of the symbolic-reduction line (E27, T3, T376); a further variant (T378) is in the backlog at low priority.

T24.title: Does a neuron-by-neuron account scale with model size?
T24.what: Blinded investigators and judges on H = 8, 16, 32 at T = 10, equal effort per size.
T24.latest: Mixed (an independent rescorer agrees). Reconstruction recovered .585 / .335 / .824 of the gap for 8 / 16 / 32 neurons; 1 of 3 fresh accounts of the 32-neuron network passes the 90% line. Judges can tell the labels apart (agreement kappa ~.92). Inferred: good labels and good reconstruction come apart. Replacing one neuron by its formula costs ~12 points at 16 neurons but ~.3 at 32, so how fragile the readout is matters more than size. Knowing the neurons' roles was not enough to calculate accuracy. Follow-up T377 is in progress.
T24.group: Neuron-level accounts and the essay question

T377.title: Follow-up to the blinded size ladder
T377.what: Follow-up to T24's mixed result on whether neuron-by-neuron accounts scale with model size.
T377.latest: Readout fragility, not model size, dominates, by a small margin (.67 against the pre-set .7 decision line). Good labels and good reconstruction come apart again; no new account passes 90%.
T377.group: Neuron-level accounts and the essay question

T6.title: Essay question: re-run of the neuron-explanation test
T6.what: Re-run of the test of 'most neurons have one job' on a 0.6B open language model with >= 100 controls and 2-3 explainers per item, to resolve the inconclusive verdict.
T6.latest: Done: neurons rated one main job 64.6% vs 20.9% for dense controls, +43.8 points [33.3, 53.7], above the 30-point bar; its controls failed their density check, which biases toward a smaller gap. Together with T383 this is ledger H-Q5, confirmed and scoped.
T6.group: Neuron-level accounts and the essay question

T383.title: Independent resolution of the essay re-run
T383.what: Resolve T6's inconclusive verdict, whose controls failed their density check.
T383.latest: Done: a different agent with its own code, controls passing their density check (median top-1 share .104): +44.6 points [36.3, 52.9]. Caveat: texture-matched controls give +37.0 [28.7, 45.5], inconclusive at the bar. Ledger H-Q5 confirmed (scoped); H-Q2 refuted for dense controls.
T383.group: Neuron-level accounts and the essay question

status_values: 'in progress' (purple box), 'negative (unverified)' (red), 'inconclusive (unverified)' (amber), 'confirmed' (green); see laneHTML() in src/page.html
